en.title: Ticket, Travel or Transport Service Complaint
en.directAnswer: Keep the ticket, booking terms, payment proof, delay or cancellation notice and any communication from the operator. Ask the operator or platform for the specific remedy available under its terms and applicable law. Do not assume every delay creates an automatic right to compensation.

atAGlance.whoFor: A passenger has a cancellation, delay, refund, seat or service dispute.
atAGlance.mainRule: Keep the ticket, booking terms, payment proof, delay or cancellation notice and any communication from the operator. Ask
atAGlance.updateStatus: Do not state a universal compensation right. Add sector-specific sources before publishing.

en.lawMeaning:
The legal route may differ for rail, bus, airline, launch or ticketing platform.

This page gives a general route. A person’s exact rights can change because of facts, documents, deadlines, legal status, court orders or later amendments.
steps: Escalate to the transport regulator/operator route.
Check DNCRP if consumer law applies.
evidence: Relevant official notices, receipts, and correspondence
en.simpleExample: A passenger arrives and learns the service is delayed for hours. They should record the scheduled time, actual information provided and any refund request rather than relying only on memory later.
commonMistakes: Assuming a refund is legally guaranteed.
blaming the ticket platform for an operator issue without checking responsibilities..
en.specialistTrigger: Serious injury; large consequential loss; aviation/rail statutory issue; group claim.
